How NightGuard AI Detects Fatigue

Combining real-time facial landmark detection, Euclidean geometry, and temporal thresholding to prevent vehicle collisions.

01

Frame Preprocessing

Captures 30 FPS video feed, resizes resolution, and normalizes brightness for low-light dashboard conditions.

02

Landmark Extraction

Locates 6 key structural coordinates around each eye region ($p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4, p_5, p_6$).

03

EAR Ratio Computation

Calculates vertical vs horizontal eye distance ratio to distinguish normal blinks from fatigue closures.

04

Staged Escalation Alarm

Tracks closure duration over time ($t \ge 2.0s$) to trigger multi-tone audio alarms before micro-sleep occurs.

Theoretical Foundation

Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR) Formula

The Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR) is a scalar value calculated from Euclidean distances between 6 2D facial landmark points mapped onto each eye. As the eye closes, vertical distances diminish to zero while horizontal distance remains constant.

EAR = ||p₂ - p₆|| + ||p₃ - p₅|| / (2 · ||p₁ - p₄||)

Computer Vision Syllabus Mapping (AML10351A)

How this project satisfies academic syllabus requirements

Unit I — Image Processing

Frame capturing, spatial scaling, RGB to grayscale conversion, histogram normalization in low-light environments.

Unit II — Segmentation

Isolating facial bounding boxes and cropping region of interest (ROI) around eyes and mouth regions.

Unit III — Object Detection

Feature extraction using Haar Cascades / MediaPipe Face Mesh for real-time facial landmark localization.

Unit IV — Geometry & 3D Vision

Euclidean metric calculations in 2D space and head pose orientation estimation for detecting head drooping.

Unit V — Machine Learning Evaluation

Precision, Recall, PERCLOS ratio computation, and latency benchmark testing across lighting conditions.

Unit VI — Safety Applications

Real-time driver assistance safety system implementation with staged audible alerts and event logging.
